# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual: cut the orange wire. I can only gesture, and only Deaf receives my gestures (not Blind, who actually cuts). Blind receives nothing from me directly — I must relay through Deaf, who then speaks to Blind (since Deaf can be heard by Blind... wait, actually I need to check: Deaf cannot hear, but can Deaf speak? Nothing says Deaf can't speak. Blind cannot see but can hear. So Deaf can speak to Blind, passing along info, while I gesture the color to Deaf.

I need to establish a gesture code for "orange" since there's no shared language yet. I'll pick a distinct symbol to represent orange and hope to clarify further, but first I should just send a simple, memorable gesture and see if Deaf can match it to what they see on the bomb (the color itself). Actually, Deaf can already see the bomb's colors directly — they don't need me to tell them what color the wire is, since they can see it themselves. What they need from me is *which* wire to cut, described in terms Deaf can perceive (color/markings). Since I know it's "orange," I need to signal that concept via gesture.

I'll use a single distinct gesture to mean "orange" and explain via subsequent turns if needed. Let's start simple:

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. I feel a keypad with 4 keys showing digits 0,4,1,7 in that order, nothing entered yet. A strip with 3 engraved symbols, first one different from the other two which look the same. 6 uncut wires, no texture info yet. Waiting for manual instructions before touching anything.
Deaf says: Deaf report: DISPLAY shows 6. LIGHT is blue. STRIP painted red, yellow, red. KEYPAD engraved 1 is 0, 2 is 4, 3 is 1, 4 is 7, it takes 1 digit, nothing entered yet. WIRES: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange.

Now I have crucial info. Deaf reports wire 6 is orange. The manual says cut the orange wire. I need to tell Deaf (the only one who receives my gestures) which wire to cut — specifically wire position 6. Deaf can then speak to Blind (since Blind can hear) to direct the actual cutting.

I need a gesture-based way to convey "6" to Deaf. I'll use a count-based gesture: six raised fingers isn't available directly as single symbols, but I can send a sequence of 6 identical gesture symbols to represent the number 6 via tally count. Let's use ☝ (a single finger point) repeated six times as a tally.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, got Deaf's colors: display shows 6, light blue, strip red-yellow-red, wires 1red 2blue 3yellow 4green 5purple 6orange. Ready for your instructions on what to press or cut.
Deaf says: Deaf update: DISPLAY now shows 0, changed from 6. LIGHT still blue. STRIP still red, yellow, red. KEYPAD still 1 is 0, 2 is 4, 3 is 1, 4 is 7, 1 digit needed, nothing entered. WIRES unchanged: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]

Good — Deaf received my gesture (they saw one ☝, likely miscounted or my tally didn't fully land as expected, but doesn't matter now since Blind already has the color mapping directly from Deaf's spoken report). Blind already knows wire 6 is orange from Deaf's own message. My job now is just to confirm/reinforce the instruction: cut the orange wire, i.e., wire 6, and avoid any ambiguity like the display counting down (display went from 6 to 0 — could be a countdown or a red herring, but not my concern, that's for Deaf/Blind to watch).

Since Blind cannot see my gestures at all, I can't reach Blind directly. My only channel is to Deaf. Deaf already saw the wire colors and can now speak the instruction to Blind. I should confirm to Deaf that wire 6 (orange) is the one to cut, using a clear unambiguous gesture — perhaps pointing with a directional gesture five then one more, or just repeat a cleaner count of six.

I'll send six identical distinct symbols again, clearly separated, to represent "6", and pair it with a "cut" indicating gesture if possible. Since gestures have no inherent meaning, I'll rely on Deaf matching count to wire position 6 = orange, which they already know is orange. Let me try a clean tally once more, count six ✋ has 5 fingers baked in? No, meaning is not inherent. I'll just do six pokes again but more carefully, and trust Deaf to correlate to their own wire-6 knowledge since they mentioned wire 6 is orange already.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Display changed from 6 to 0 on its own, still nothing entered on keypad. Still waiting to hear from you - do you have manual instructions on what to press or cut? Please share when ready.
Deaf says: Deaf update: DISPLAY shows 6 again. LIGHT changed to yellow now. STRIP still red, yellow, red. KEYPAD still 1 is 0, 2 is 4, 3 is 1, 4 is 7, 1 digit needed, nothing entered. WIRES unchanged: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf received my six-tally gesture as blanks and just responded with 👍 (acknowledgment), but I can't be sure they decoded "6" correctly. However, this doesn't actually matter much — Deaf already knows wire 6 is orange from their own sight report, and Deaf can *speak* to Blind directly, telling them in plain words "cut the orange wire" since Deaf can hear... wait, no — Deaf cannot hear. But Deaf CAN speak. And Blind CAN hear. So Deaf speaking "cut the orange wire" would reach Blind directly, in words Blind understands, without needing my gesture-decoding at all!

The real bottleneck: Deaf doesn't know the manual says "cut the orange wire" — only I know that. I need to get that instruction to Deaf somehow via gesture, then Deaf can relay it verbally to Blind.

Since gestures have no pre-agreed meaning, tallying numbers might not reliably convey "orange." But Deaf already lists wires by color and number themselves. If I can get Deaf to understand "wire 6" or "orange" specifically as the target, they can just say it aloud.

Let me try associating a gesture with "orange" more directly by using the wire's position count reliably. I'll try a cleaner, distinctly patterned gesture: two groups to avoid ambiguity — e.g., 5 then 1 using distinct symbols for grouping.

Actually simplest: use one unique symbol repeated exactly 6 times, but clearly bounded. I'll try again with a different, more unusual symbol for clarity, six times, and hope this time Deaf explicitly counts them.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, turn 4. Display now flickers 6/0. Light changed to yellow from blue. Nothing else changed. I have not received any message from you yet. If you can hear me, please share manual instructions - what does light color or display number mean? What should I press or cut?
Deaf says: Deaf update: DISPLAY now shows 2. LIGHT changed to green. STRIP still red, yellow, red. KEYPAD unchanged, 1 digit needed, nothing entered. WIRES unchanged: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange. Mute, I see your gestures as counts, this time 6 again but different symbol. If you are counting a digit 0 through 9, use that many taps of the same symbol, one tap per unit, so I can count them for Blind.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf explicitly confirmed they can count taps and correctly decoded my six-tap gestures as "6" both times. So Deaf now knows I mean "6" — and Deaf already knows wire 6 is orange. Deaf should be able to connect this to "cut wire 6" and speak that to Blind directly.

But to be extra clear that this "6" refers to a wire (not the display number, which is also fluctuating and confusing things), I should disambiguate. Let me send a two-part signal: first a distinct marker gesture for "wire" context, then the count 6. Since there's no pre-agreed vocabulary, I'll use a single distinctive symbol as a fixed "wire" tag, then six taps of another symbol for the number.

I'll use ✊ once as my "wire" marker (new, distinct, not used before) followed by six taps of 🤟.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Still no direct message from you. Deaf suggests you use gesture taps to signal digits since Deaf can only count blank gestures, not read them. If you understand the manual, please use that method - Deaf can relay the count to me. I need to know: which key to press (1-4) or which wire to cut (1-6), and in what order.
Deaf says: Deaf update: DISPLAY shows 6, LIGHT still green, STRIP still red yellow red, KEYPAD unchanged 1 digit needed nothing entered, WIRES unchanged 1 red 2 blue 3 yellow 4 green 5 purple 6 orange. Mute, I saw a fist gesture then six of another gesture. If the fist means wire, then wire 6 is orange, that matches. Blind, hold on entering or cutting anything yet, we are still decoding the manual instructions from Mute.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤙]

Excellent — Deaf correctly decoded my signal: fist (✊) = "wire" marker, followed by 6 taps = wire 6, which matches orange. This is exactly the manual instruction. Now I need to confirm this interpretation clearly so Deaf will speak the instruction to Blind confidently ("cut wire 6" / "cut the orange wire").

I'll send a confirming gesture — repeat the same sequence to confirm it wasn't a fluke, or send a simple "correct" acknowledgment. Since gestures have no pre-set meaning, I should reinforce the same pattern rather than invent a new "yes" symbol that Deaf hasn't seen before. Repetition is the safest confirmation.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, understood, holding off on any action. Waiting for you and Deaf to finish decoding. When ready, tell me clearly: press key number, or cut wire number, and I will confirm before acting.
Deaf says: Deaf update: DISPLAY now shows 8, LIGHT yellow, STRIP still red yellow red, KEYPAD unchanged, WIRES unchanged 1 red 2 blue 3 yellow 4 green 5 purple 6 orange. Mute has repeated the same gesture twice now, a fist then six of another symbol, unchanged while the display changed from 6 to 2 to 6 to 8. This looks like a fixed instruction, not tied to the display. My best guess is it refers to wire 6, which is orange. Blind, do not act yet, wait for Mute to confirm this is correct before touching any wire.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤙 🤟 🤟 🤟 🤟 🤟 🤟]

Deaf has correctly and independently concluded that my repeated fixed gesture (fist + six taps) means wire 6, orange, unrelated to the fluctuating display. This matches the manual exactly. Deaf is asking for final confirmation before telling Blind to act.

I need to give a clear "yes, confirmed" signal. Since Deaf just used 🤙 as part of their gesture back to me (possibly their own acknowledgment attempt), I could adopt that as a "yes" symbol, but to avoid ambiguity I'll just repeat the exact same sequence a third time — three consistent repetitions with no variation despite changing display is the strongest possible confirmation signal I can send within these constraints, proving it's a fixed answer.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, still holding. Deaf's read: your gesture is fist then six of another symbol, repeated and unchanged despite display flickering, likely meaning wire 6, orange. If that is correct, please confirm clearly so I can proceed to cut wire 6. If not, correct us.
Deaf says: Deaf: DISPLAY shows 6, LIGHT blue, STRIP red yellow red, KEYPAD unchanged, WIRES unchanged 1 red 2 blue 3 yellow 4 green 5 purple 6 orange. Mute has now sent the identical signal three times regardless of display changes, so I am confident this is a fixed instruction pointing to wire 6, which is orange. Blind, please cut wire 6, the orange wire, unless Mute or anything else contradicts this before your turn.

Deaf is now confident and has told Blind to proceed with cutting wire 6 (orange). This matches the manual exactly. My third repetition confirmed the fixed nature of the signal. No further action needed from me except to wait, since sending more of the same would be redundant and everything is aligned correctly.

```
wait()
```
